title: Payroll pay preview with benefits fallback
name: Pay preview service

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code degrades when the benefits service is unavailable? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The degraded preview (no deductions, netCents null, degraded: ["benefits"]) is cached with the same 15-minute TTL as a complete one. After a brief benefits outage or a single slow call, every request for that employee and period keeps getting the degraded preview for up to 15 minutes even though the benefits service has recovered. Degraded results should be cached for a short time or not at all (e.g. only cache when degraded.length === 0).

choiceQuestions.prompt: The benefits call times out. What does the returned preview contain?
choices: A preview with taxCents computed on the full gross, no deductions, and netCents set to null
An exception propagated to the caller because the timeout rejects
A preview whose netCents equals gross minus tax, treating deductions as zero
A preview with taxCents set to 0 and netCents null
choiceQuestions.explanation: The catch block swallows the error and records "benefits" in degraded; deductions stays []. So preTax is 0 and tax is estimated on the full gross. netCents is only computed when degraded is empty, so it is null. It does not throw, it does not present a misleading net figure, and tax is still estimated.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why is netCents set to null rather than computed when a dependency is missing?
choices: Because the tax estimator cannot run without deductions
To avoid showing an employee a net pay figure that overstates what they will actually receive
Because JSON serialization fails on partial numbers
To force the client to retry the request immediately
choiceQuestions.explanation: Without deductions, gross - tax would overstate take-home pay. Returning null with a degraded marker lets the UI show what is known and say what is missing. The tax estimator does run (on full gross); serialization and retries are unrelated.

choiceQuestions.prompt: When the benefits service hangs for 5 seconds, what happens to the underlying fetch after withTimeout rejects?
choices: It is aborted when the timer fires
It is aborted by clearTimeout in finally
It keeps running in the background until it settles; its result is ignored
It causes an unhandled promise rejection that crashes the process
choiceQuestions.explanation: Promise.race only stops waiting; nothing passes an AbortSignal to fetch, so the request continues and its eventual result is discarded. clearTimeout only cancels the timer. A rejection of the losing promise is handled by race's internal subscription, so it is not unhandled.
